run.display_title: test: do not assert a HEAD response body through inject() (#7148)

head_commit.message:
test: do not assert a HEAD response body through inject() (#7148)

Two tests read the body of a HEAD response through `fastify.inject()`:

- "Should allow registering a constrained GET route after a constrained
HEAD route" (`test/constrained-routes.test.js`) checks `res.payload ===
'custom HEAD response'`;
- "fastify.all should add all the methods to the same url"
(`test/internals/all.test.js`) parses the HEAD payload as JSON.

A real server sends no body for HEAD, and fastify/light-my-request#408
makes `inject()` do the same. @gurgunday approved the behaviour there
but asked for fastify core to be updated before it ships, since these
two tests would fail with it.

These tests now check the response headers instead of the body:

- The constrained route test asserts the `content-type` set by the
custom HEAD handler (`text/plain`) and the `content-length` of `'custom
HEAD response'`. That still shows the custom handler ran, not a HEAD
route derived from the GET one.
- The `fastify.all` test asserts the HEAD response's `content-length`
matches `JSON.stringify({ method: 'HEAD' })` and parses the body only
for the other methods.

Both files pass with the current light-my-request release and with the
#408 branch symlinked into `node_modules` (26 tests each time), so this
can land before or after it. ESLint is clean on both files.

(cherry picked from commit 78d68b2225baa3b7e05ebb5522239f40a4bcf6e8)

run.display_title: fix: handle web Response in auto-exposed HEAD route

head_commit.message:
fix: handle web Response in auto-exposed HEAD route

Fastify auto-exposes a HEAD route for each GET route and supports returning a
web Response from a handler. When a GET handler returned a Response, a HEAD
request to that route crashed with HTTP 500: headRouteOnSendHandler runs in the
onSend phase, before reply.js unwraps the Response, so it received the raw
Response object (which matches neither the node stream nor the web stream
guard) and reached Buffer.byteLength, which throws on a Response.

The HEAD onSend handler now recognises a web Response and mirrors reply.js:
applies the Response status and headers, rejects an already-consumed body with
FST_ERR_REP_RESPONSE_BODY_CONSUMED (same as GET, so HEAD does not silently
succeed where GET fails), otherwise cancels the ReadableStream and sends an
empty body. A HEAD request now behaves like the equivalent GET.

head_commit.message:
fix: handle web Response in auto-exposed HEAD route

Fastify auto-exposes a HEAD route for each GET route and supports returning a
web Response from a handler. When a GET handler returned a Response, a HEAD
request to that route crashed with HTTP 500: headRouteOnSendHandler runs in the
onSend phase, before reply.js unwraps the Response, so it received the raw
Response object (which matches neither the node stream nor the web stream
guard) and reached Buffer.byteLength, which throws on a Response.

The HEAD onSend handler now recognises a web Response and mirrors reply.js:
applies the Response status and headers, rejects an already-consumed body with
FST_ERR_REP_RESPONSE_BODY_CONSUMED (same as GET, so HEAD does not silently
succeed where GET fails), otherwise cancels the ReadableStream and sends an
empty body. A HEAD request now behaves like the equivalent GET.

Adds tests: a GET route returning a Response is stripped to an empty body on
HEAD (200, headers preserved, content-length parity with GET), and a consumed
Response body errors on HEAD exactly as on GET.

head_commit.message:
Fix: key the reply serializer cache by httpStatus and contentType

compileSerializationSchema passes httpStatus and contentType to the serializer
compiler, so a serializer compiled for one pair is not interchangeable with
another. The cache was keyed by the schema object alone, so reusing a schema with
different metadata returned the serializer compiled for the first call and the
compiler never saw the new values.

Store the serializers for a schema in a Map keyed by the metadata tuple, and keep
the WeakMap keyed by schema as the outer level. An omitted value is distinguished
from an explicit undefined or null so the key stays stable.

getSerializationFunction is called without metadata by callers that want the
schema's serializer. When only one serializer has been compiled for that schema
there is no ambiguity, so return it; otherwise the caller has to name the pair.

Refs #6987

head_commit.message:
fix: prevent context leak in stream_with_context on cross-thread GC

When a client disconnects mid-stream, the WSGI server abandons the
body iterator. The generator is finalized by the garbage collector,
often on a different thread than the one that pushed the context.
ctx.pop() raises RuntimeError because the context is not active
on the GC thread, leaving the context stuck on the original thread.

Replace `with ctx:` with manual push()/pop() in the generator, and
catch the RuntimeError from cross-thread pop() to properly reset
the context state (_push_count and _cv_token).

Fixes #6123

* fix(h2): replay requests whose HEADERS raced a GOAWAY

head_commit.message:
fix(fetch): preserve abort propagation after garbage collection

Copied and cloned requests can lose cancellation after garbage collection
because their signals do not keep forwarding controllers alive.

Native AbortSignal composition can retain finalization records while a
long-lived source survives on supported Node.js versions.

For 5,000 constructor copies of one retained parent, Node 24.20.0 / V8
13.6.233.17-node.53 improves from 35.37 us to 0.83 us per copy.
Two fresh processes use 50,000 warm-up operations and seven trials,
discarding the fastest and slowest.

Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/62363

run.display_title: fix(http2): keep persistent error sink on released streams (#5983)

head_commit.message:
fix(http2): keep persistent error sink on released streams (#5983)

* fix(http2): keep persistent error sink on released streams

When an HTTP/2 session is torn down with an error (e.g. the idle reaper
in onHttp2SessionIdleTimeout), Node fans that error out to every native
stream still tracked in the session's internal state. A released stream
that no longer has an 'error' listener then crashes the process with an
unhandled `InformationalError: socket idle timeout` (#5936).

releaseRequestStream, severRequestStream and releaseUpgradeStream only
installed a one-shot `once('error', noop)` sink (and not at all in
onError), so a single late error consumed it and the subsequent
session-level error went unhandled.

Keep a persistent `on('error', noop)` sink on every stream undici stops
tracking, and add a noop fallback in onError when the real handler is
removed. Retain the sink on upgrade streams instead of dropping it in
onUpgradeStreamClose.

Closes #5936.

* test(http2): make idle reaper regression test cross-platform robust

The released stream is only observable in the window between its 'end' and
'close' events. On some platforms (Node 25/macOS) that window is too short to
inspect, so the previous synchronous assertion failed CI. Poll briefly for the
released stream and skip the test when the teardown race cannot be observed,
instead of failing. The test still fails on the buggy implementation whenever
the window is observable.

head_commit.message:
fix(cache): ignore SQLITE_BUSY in the sqlite cache store (#6049)

The store is meant to be shared between processes. SQLite reports a
database another connection is writing as SQLITE_BUSY/SQLITE_LOCKED
("database is locked"), and those errors currently propagate out of
get(), set(), delete() and the pruning that set() performs, failing the
request that triggered the write.

Caching is best effort, so skip the operation instead of throwing: a
locked database is a cache miss, and the next request retries.

run.display_title: fix(h2): replace a connection that stops responding after a stream timeout

head_commit.message:
fix(h2): replace a connection that stops responding after a stream timeout

A stream timeout only reset that stream, unlike HTTP/1.1 which destroys
the socket. When the connection itself silently died (dropped by a NAT or
load balancer, a hung peer), every new request was sent on it and timed
out in turn, and the Pool never opened a new connection.

On a stream timeout, send a PING and stop opening streams on the session
until it is acked. If no ack arrives within the timeout that fired, reset
the session so queued requests move to a fresh connection.

run.display_title: [v6.x] fix: handle frozen globalThis in setGlobalDispatcher (#5574)

head_commit.message:
fix: handle frozen globalThis in setGlobalDispatcher (#5574)

* fix: handle frozen globalThis in setGlobalDispatcher

When Object.freeze(globalThis) is called before undici globals are accessed,
setGlobalDispatcher would throw TypeError because it cannot extend globalThis.

This fix wraps the Object.defineProperty calls in try/catch. When globalThis
is not extensible (frozen), the dispatcher is stored in a module-level
fallback variable instead. getGlobalDispatcher is updated to return the
fallback dispatcher when the globalThis property is not available.

This allows undici to work correctly even when globalThis has been frozen,
which is recommended by Node.js security best practices (CWE-349).

Fixes issue where Object.freeze(globalThis) breaks undici access.

* test: add unit test for frozen globalThis in setGlobalDispatcher

Add comprehensive test coverage for the frozen globalThis fix. Tests verify:
1. setGlobalDispatcher does not throw when globalThis is frozen
2. getGlobalDispatcher continues to return a valid dispatcher
3. The fallback mechanism works correctly when globalThis is not extensible

This addresses the review feedback from mcollina requesting tests.

* test: improve frozen globalThis test coverage

Add comprehensive test cases to ensure all code paths in the frozen globalThis
fix are exercised. Tests verify:
1. setGlobalDispatcher does not throw when globalThis is frozen
2. getGlobalDispatcher returns a valid dispatcher
3. Fallback dispatcher persists across multiple calls

This addresses review feedback requesting tests.

(cherry picked from commit a0922b0b6b5db878881017abb6fca3bbcdea555a)

run.display_title: [v6.x] fix(fetch): error the stream when decompression fails after onComplete

head_commit.message:
fix(fetch): error the stream when decompression fails after onComplete

The body pull loop runs decompression after onComplete has already
fired, but onComplete removed the fetch controller's 'terminated'
listener (onAborted). When zlib fails (e.g. a response declares
content-encoding: gzip but the body is not valid gzip), controller
termination never reaches the response stream, so text(), json() and
stream reads hang forever and the AbortSignal cannot end them.

Register the onAborted listener only once per fetch (guarded by the
presence of fetchParams.controller.resume) and stop removing it in
onComplete. This keeps the listener alive until the fetch settles so a
late decompression failure correctly errors the stream, while avoiding
the MaxListenersExceededWarning on redirects that the single
registration prevents.

Fixes https://github.com/nodejs/undici/issues/5999

Backport of #3754.

Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/pull/3754

run.display_title: Backport upgrade diagnostics lifecycle fixes to v6.x (#5833)

head_commit.message:
Backport upgrade diagnostics lifecycle fixes to v6.x (#5833)

* fix: complete upgrade diagnostics lifecycle

Successful CONNECT and protocol upgrades stop before Undici marks the request complete. Diagnostics subscribers retain request state, and streamed request-body listeners remain attached to the upgraded socket.

Publish the existing response lifecycle around accepted upgrades. Preserve the early HTTP/2 CONNECT handoff in v6, and terminate diagnostics if the stream fails before its response.

Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/pull/5783
Signed-off-by: Ruben Bridgewater <ruben.bridgewater@datadoghq.com>

* fix: preserve abort after upgrade handoff

Completing upgrade requests suppresses late request errors, but v6 retains the abort callback as the transport cleanup owner after handoff. Returning early leaves upgraded sockets and HTTP/2 CONNECT streams open.

Signed-off-by: Ruben Bridgewater <ruben.bridgewater@datadoghq.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Ruben Bridgewater <ruben.bridgewater@datadoghq.com>

run.display_title: [v6.x] fix(fetch): don't append a duplicate content-length header (#5060)

head_commit.message:
fix(fetch): don't append a duplicate content-length header

Backport of the fetch part of #5060 to v6.x. When a request already carries
a caller-set Content-Length, fetch appended its own computed value, producing
e.g. "36, 36". undici 6's own core tolerated that via parseInt, but undici 6's
fetch is commonly dispatched through Node's bundled undici (>= 7.28 on Node
24.18+, the v8 Dispatcher1Wrapper on Node 26) via the shared global dispatcher,
which rejects it with "invalid content-length header".

The strict validator from #5060 is intentionally not backported.

run.display_title: Fix: Prevent query parameter corruption in base_url

head_commit.message:
Fix query parameter corruption in base_url with trailing slash enforcement

When a base_url contained query parameters, _enforce_trailing_slash() was
appending a slash to the entire raw_path (including the query string), which
corrupted the query parameter values.

For example:
- Before: base_url="https://api.com?data=1" became "https://api.com?data=1/"
  (query param corrupted to "data=1/" instead of "data=1")
- After: base_url="https://api.com?data=1" becomes "https://api.com/?data=1"
  (query param correctly preserved as "data=1")

The fix splits the raw_path into path and query components, adds the trailing
slash only to the path portion, then recombines them.

Fixes #3614

the original http method to GET when following redirects, some server
applications expects the "legacy" behavior which keeps the same method
over redirects.

Add new option to clients to select the behavior.
